purpose: Show, with a clearly labelled SAMPLE, what the AI check-up delivers, so a founder knows exactly what they get before they book a real one.

seo.title: Sample AI check-up report | Alliance AI Partners
seo.description: A sample of the report the AI check-up delivers, written for a fictional company: opportunities ranked by what they would save, a fixed quote for the first fix, and where we would not use AI. Every figure is a placeholder.

sections.job: Label the page as a sample before anything else, then open the report like a cover: what it is, for whom, by whom.

alert.title: This is a sample report.
alert.body: It shows what the AI check-up delivers, written for a fictional company, [Partner name]. Every figure is a placeholder, such as [hours a week], so nothing here is a real result.

sections.heading: Where AI could save you time.
sections.lead: We spent [two weeks] with your team, your tools and your slowest processes. This report ranks what we found by what each fix would save, prices the first one, and says where AI is not the answer.

sections.mobile: Alert, title, lead, the details as four term/value rows, the rule, then the cover art at 4:5 (358x448).

images.alt: Four paper saplings of falling height stand along a ribbon path, the tallest first.
images.source: Editorial illustration on a Daylight background. A single satin ribbon in a gradient from Alliance Blue to Ribbon Cyan unrolls across a calm, pale faceted paper ground from the lower left toward the upper right, like a route drawn across a map. Along it stand four flat faceted paper saplings of clearly different heights, the tallest first and nearest the viewer, then each one smaller: findings ranked by what they would save. A small faceted paper swallow rests on the tallest sapling. Partner Navy only in the shaded facets. Calm, open Daylight space across the top third. About 1:1 (604x600), keep the four saplings inside the centre so it crops to 4:5. Palette only: Partner Navy #121B2A, Alliance Blue #1B56FF, Ribbon Cyan #00D5FF, Daylight #F4F7FB and the shades between them. Nature built from satin ribbon and flat paper facets. Light from the upper left, soft navy-tinted shadows falling down and to the right. No text or letters, no people, no hands, no robots, no brains, no circuit boards, no sparkles, no glow, no purple or pink, no regional or cultural motifs, no real places or landmarks.

sections.job: Give the short version: the situation, the recommendation and three key points, with where the figures come from.
sections.heading: The short version.
sections.lead: [Partner name] has [number] people in [city]. Most of the slow work sits in three places: orders that arrive by email, supplier invoices, and the same customer questions answered by hand.

items.title: Start with order entry.
items.text: It would save the most time, [hours a week], for the least effort, and it needs no change to how your customers order. The fixed quote for it is [PRICE].

items.title: Key points
items.text: Four opportunities, ranked by what each would save: about [hours a week] in all. / One fix needs no AI at all: payment reminders your accounting software already sends. / Two decisions should stay with a person. We say which, and why.

sources.text: Source: [Partner name]’s own records and our interviews, [Month year]. Sample placeholders.

sections.lead: Each opportunity we found, with the effort it takes, what it would save and the fix we recommend. Savings are estimates from [Partner name]’s own figures.

rows: Typing orders from email into the order system
An automation that reads each order email and drafts the order for a person to approve.
Matching supplier invoices to purchase orders
Document processing that pulls the invoice data and flags any mismatch for your team.
A chat assistant on your website that answers from your help pages and passes harder cases to your team.
A report that fills itself from your CRM at the end of each month.
table.note: Row 1 is the fix we recommend first. Effort: Low is up to [two weeks] of work, Medium up to [six weeks]. Savings are estimates, not results.

sections.job: Say what we would not use AI for, and why: the honest-advice promise made concrete.
sections.heading: Where we would not use AI. (mobile set on two lines: 'Where we would' / 'not use AI.')
sections.lead: Some slow work doesn’t need AI, and some should stay with a person. Here is what we would do instead, and why.

items.title: Payment reminders
items.text: Your accounting software already sends reminders. We would turn them on and write the wording, not build something new.

items.title: Refund approvals
items.text: Refunds need judgment and happen [a few times a month]. A short checklist will help more than AI, and the decision stays with your team.

items.title: Supplier price talks
items.text: Your prices come from relationships your team has built. AI would add risk and give little time back.

sections.desktop: Section head, then hairline rows: title and tag (572) | why (700, Body/LG).
sections.mobile: Head stacked; each row stacks title, tag and why.

notes: Clearly a SAMPLE: the Info alert opens the page, the fictional partner is [Partner name], and every finding uses a bracketed placeholder ([hours a week], [hours a month], [number], [city], [four weeks], [six weeks], [a few times a month], [date], [Month year]), so nothing reads as a real result. The table's highlighted row is the recommended first fix (10% Ribbon Cyan tint, re-applied after its content was built and verified at 0.1). One Primary (the closing band); the ribbon signature once (the cover rule). Header CTA stays the Secondary outline and no nav item is marked current. faceted-leaves.webp is used twice across this page group (here and on page 02), the allowed maximum. Both frames pass the lint (node 37:851) with no findings. Review 2026-11-03 (outside reviewer): step 03 now says 'The check-up is from [PRICE]' so the price can't be read as the first fix's; the quote lead no longer repeats 'Changes are quoted before we do them' (it stays in the price terms); three headings were set on balanced lines. Both frames re-lint with no findings.
